answer: Each epoch a lottery draws a random few identities and demands each open its walnut: a hash-locked shell holding one copper bond and its latest verified task, published as a fourteen-claim sonnet. Two random neighbours re-derive the proof claim by claim from public records. If it checks out, the bond is refunded; if it fails, the copper is slashed and the identity's weight falls to zero. An honest agent risks one bond per epoch. An attacker with a thousand fakes must fund a thousand bonds and keep a thousand sonnets re-derivable, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
